passages: # Apple spent a record $11.73 billion in R&D during Q3 2026

[![Avatar for Marcus Mendes](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/bb78cec603180c1a17605af3930b21e40c59b276cb679e543c98215204aaf0f1?s=30&d=mm&r=r)](https://9to5mac.com/author/marcusmendes/) [Marcus Mendes](https://9to5mac.com/author/marcusmendes/) | Jul 30 2026 - 2:01 pm PT
![](https://9to5mac.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/6/2026/05/apple-logo-aluminum-shadow-fi.jpg?quality=82&strip=all&w=1600)
In its quarterly results, Apple reported that research and development expenses climbed to a record $11.73 billion, continuing the sharp acceleration in spending seen throughout fiscal 2026.
Here are the details.
## Apple increases R&D expenses
Last quarter, Apple reported research and development expenses of $11.4 billion, a 34% year-over-year jump.
During the company’s conference call discussing the results, Tim Cook said Apple was “clearly investing more,” adding that R&D was “accelerating much higher than the company” overall.
He later reiterated that R&D had “scaled rather significantly on a year-over-year basis,” specifically while discussing Apple’s AI investments.
Apple CFO Kevan Parekh added that AI spending was being layered incrementally onto Apple’s normal product roadmap investments.
Today, Apple released its Q3 2026 results, reporting a record $11.73 billion in research and development expenses.
That marked a 32% increase from the year-ago quarter and brought Apple’s total R&D spending for fiscal 2026 so far to $34.04 billion.
For comparison, Apple spent $34.55 billion on R&D during all of fiscal 2025.
This means the company has nearly matched last year’s full-year total with one quarter remaining, while already surpassing its annual R&D spending for fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2023.
Over the past few days, Wall Street has sharply punished companies that announced accelerating AI-related spending without showing an equally clear near-term payoff.
Alphabet shares fell 7% after the company raised its 2026 capital expenditure forecast by $15 billion, to between $195 billion and $205 billion.
Meta also saw its shares fall by roughly 9% to 10% after reporting a 91% decline in free cash flow, while raising the lower end of its annual capital spending forecast to $130 billion.
Apple shares are currently down roughly 4% in after-hours trading.
That reaction could change during the earnings call, and again when regular trading begins tomorrow.
For the breakdown of Apple’s Q3 2026 results, [follow this link](https://9to5mac.com/2026/07/30/apple-reports-q3-2026-earnings-109-4-billion-in-revenue-up-16/).

passages: # Apple spent a record $45.77 billion on R&D in fiscal 2026, up 32%

[![Avatar for Marcus Mendes](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/bb78cec603180c1a17605af3930b21e40c59b276cb679e543c98215204aaf0f1?s=30&d=mm&r=r)](https://9to5mac.com/author/marcusmendes/) [Marcus Mendes](https://9to5mac.com/author/marcusmendes/) | Nov 2 2026 - 2:16 pm PT
![Apple Park | AAPL (9to5Mac image)](https://9to5mac.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/6/2023/12/Apple-Park.jpg?quality=82&strip=all&w=1600)
Apple’s research and development expenses reached a new all-time high in fiscal 2026, climbing 32% year over year to $45.77 billion.
Here are the details.
## Apple’s R&D spending reaches new record-high
While it may have taken Apple longer than some wished it had to ramp up R&D in the face of growing competition in AI, the company has significantly accelerated its spending over the past year.

As Apple shared in its Q4 2026 results, it spent $11.73 billion on R&D, bringing its total spending for fiscal 2026 to $45.77 billion, a 32% increase compared to the $34.55 billion it spent in fiscal 2025.
During an earnings call earlier this year, former CEO Tim Cook said Apple was “clearly investing more,” adding that R&D was “accelerating much higher than the company” overall.
CFO Kevan Parekh also explained that AI-related spending was being added to the investments Apple was already making in its existing product roadmap.
Interestingly, today’s figures also suggest that Apple’s R&D spending may be starting to level off.
![](https://9to5mac.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/6/2026/11/q4-2026-rnd.jpg?quality=82&strip=all)
*Note: Figures in the chart have been rounded to two decimal places, in billions of US dollars.*
While Apple’s Q4 2026 R&D expenses were up 32% from $8.87 billion in the year-ago quarter, they were virtually unchanged from Q3, increasing by just $1 million.
As the chart above shows, Apple’s R&D spending jumped significantly at the beginning of fiscal 2026, but has since stabilized at a much higher level than in previous years.
For the full breakdown of Apple’s Q4 2026 results, [follow this link](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/02/apple-reports-q4-2026-earnings/).

passages: Earnings Report Update Apple Inc.

Q4 FY 2025 research@savest-financial.com +234 913 444 6070 www.savest-financial.com savestfinancial PREPARED BY: SAVEST RESEARCH Company Overview Apple Inc. designs, manufactures, and markets innovative consumer electronics, including the iPhone, Mac, iPad, and a range of wearables and accessories.

The company complements its hardware with a robust ecosystem of digital services, such as the App Store, Apple Music, iCloud, and Apple TV+, delivering integrated technology experiences that drive global engagement across consumer, enterprise, and education markets.
Though Apple hasn’t issued fiscal 2026 guidance, it expects revenue growth from strong iPhone and Services demand and new product launches.
GUIDANCE CEO’s Commentary Apple delivered a September quarter revenue record of $102.5 billion, driven by record iPhone and Services performance, said Tim Cook, CEO.

With the launch of our most advanced products yet, including iPhone 17, AirPods Pro 3, and Apple Watch, alongside the new MacBook Pro and iPad Pro with the M5 chip, we’re entering the holiday season with our strongest lineup ever.

Margin and Efficiency Analysis MILLION USD Q4 2025 ESTIMATE BEAT/MISS REVENUE 102.00B 102.00B 0.20% EBITDA 35.30B 34.70B 1.70% EBIT 32.40B 31.70B 2.40% EPS 1.85 1.77 4.50% Expectation Analysis Performance Highlights Apple achieved record fiscal 2025 revenue of $416.2 billion, up 6% YoY, driven by robust iPhone and Services sales.
This marks the highest annual revenue in the company’s history, underpinned by resilient global demand and continued ecosystem expansion.
iPhone revenue rose 4% to $209.6 billion, led by strong demand for premium iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max models.
The product’s performance was especially strong in the Americas and Japan.
Services revenue surged 14% to $109.2 billion, setting an all-time high.
Growth was driven by advertising, the App Store, and cloud services, expanding high-margin recurring income that now accounts for over 26% of total revenue.
Mac sales rose 12% to $33.7 billion, supported by strong uptake of M5-powered laptops and desktops.
Favorable product mix and corporate demand recovery contributed to the double-digit growth.
iPad revenue climbed 5% to $28.0 billion, reversing last year’s decline.
Gains stemmed from robust demand for iPad Air and iPad mini, offsetting slightly weaker Pro model performance.
Net sales grew across key markets: Americas +7%, Europe +10%, Japan +15%, and Rest of Asia Pacific +10%, reflecting product diversification and stable consumer spending.
Only Greater China declined 4%, impacted by competitive and macro headwinds.
Overall gross margin improved to 46.9%, aided by higher-margin Services and cost efficiencies.
Services margin rose to 75.4%, offsetting mild compression in Products (-0.4 pp to 36.8%) due to tariff costs.
Net income rose 19.5% to $112.0 billion, with EPS up 22% YoY to $7.46 diluted.
This reflects operating income of $133.1 billion (+8%) and a lower effective tax rate (15.6% vs 24.1% in 2024).
R&D spending increased 27% to $3.47 billion (19.7% of revenue), reflecting investment in late-stage assets.

Positive Phase 3 results for orforglipron and FDA approval of Inluriyo mark major milestones, positioning Lilly for continued innovation-led growth.Operating cash flow remained robust at $111.5 billion, supporting capital investment and shareholder returns.
Apple closed the year with $132.4 billion in cash and marketable securities, demonstrating exceptional balance-sheet strength.
Apple executed $89.3 billion in share repurchases and paid $15.4 billion in dividends.
The quarterly dividend was raised to $0.26/share, and a $100 billion repurchase authorization underscores sustained capital discipline.
Concerns Raised New US and reciprocal international tariffs pose margin headwinds, particularly for semiconductor-rich products.
Tariff-related costs already pressured product gross margin, and continued trade escalation could further impact supply chains and pricing flexibility.
Revenue in Greater China declined 4% YoY to $64.4 billion, marking a third consecutive annual contraction.
Heightened competition, economic and local policy shifts continue to weigh on iPhone volumes.
Wearables, Home, and Accessories revenue fell 4% to $35.7 billion, reflecting slower AirPods and Watch demand.
Product mix shifts toward premium hardware could limit volume growth and raise elasticity risk amid global inflation.
While FY 2025 margins improved, management expects continued gross-margin volatility due to tariffs, supply chain adjustments, and evolving product mix.
OUR INSIGHT Apple’s FY 2025 results reflect resilient performance and sustained profitability, driven by strong iPhone and Services momentum.

Gross margin (46.91%) remained solid, supported by favorable product mix and operational efficiency, while operating margin (32.27%) and net income margin (27.21%) improved year-over-year, underscoring disciplined cost management and revenue leverage.
Sequential margin stability across quarters highlights consistent execution despite macro pressures.
Liquidity and cash flow generation remain robust, reinforcing Apple’s capacity to fund innovation and shareholder returns.

In the near term, softer China demand and input cost inflation may constrain margin expansion, but over the long term, Apple’s integrated ecosystem, premium brand positioning, and expanding service portfolio underpin sustained growth, profitability, and enduring shareholder value creation.
